card.title: MOSQUITO B Mk IV
card.text: At the end of turn, Convert into MOSQUITO F Mk II.
card.flavorText: The de Havilland DH.98 Mosquito was a British twin-engined, multirole combat aircraft that was introduced during WWII. Its airframe was constructed mostly of wood, hence its nickname "Wooden Wonder", or "Mossie". When it became operational in 1941 it was the fastest operational aircraft in the world. The B Mk IV series of the Mosquito were bomber variants that came into service in 1942 and 273 were built. The 1st series of the variant had a payload of four 110 kg bombs, but the 2nd series increased the payload to four 230 kg bombs. In April 1943, a decision was made to modify a B Mk IV to carry a 1,800 kg Blockbuster bomb, commonly referred to as "cookie." Several Mosquito B Mk IVs were also modified to carry the Highball bouncing bomb, a smaller version of the one used in the “Dambusters” raid, and intended for attacks on enemy ships. Early missions of the B Mk IV variant included raids over Germany and German occupied territories with the intent of straining enemy morale. The Mosquito’s bombing capabilities were also demonstrated in a raid on the Gestapo headquarters in Oslo in September 1942.
